subject: [BE] Hosts for the deployables on .NET 10: commerce, access, operations and workers, each composing its modules
description: Hosts for the deployables on .NET 10: commerce, access, operations and workers, each composing its modules. In **ticvai-backend**, on .NET 10 LTS (decided 30 September; ADR-0055). Four .NET hosts in one solution: commerce (Identity, Tenancy, Catalogue, Order, Ledger, Wallet), access (Access), operations (F&B, Retail, Inventory, VenueOps, Marketing, WhiteLabel, Reporting, Platform, CrossRegion) and workers (the outbox relay, every module's event consumers, scheduled jobs), each composing its modules through IModule. ticvai-ai stays the Python service. Done when: each host starts locally with its modules registered and a health endpoint, CI builds one image per host, and moving a module to another host is a change of one registration.

subject: [BE] Qdrant cluster in dev and staging: 3 nodes, TLS, snapshots, monitoring
description: Qdrant cluster in dev and staging: 3 nodes, TLS, snapshots, monitoring. In **ticvai-infra** (Terraform): a self-hosted 3-node Qdrant cluster in Azure UAE North for dev and staging (ADR-0049), pinned to 1.16 or later, with TLS, JWT RBAC on and the signing key in the cell's Key Vault, snapshot storage in the UAE, and monitoring and alerts on node health, disk and latency. Check Qdrant Hybrid Cloud on our own AKS as an alternative before building. Done when: the cluster survives the loss of one node, a snapshot of a test collection restores into a fresh cluster, and a request without a valid token is refused.

subject: [BE] Per-tenant request budgets: a token bucket per tenant and audience, and a load-aware share per replica
description: Per-tenant request budgets: a token bucket per tenant and audience, and a load-aware share per replica. ADR-0064 (accepted 1 October), in the kernel middleware of the commerce, access and operations hosts: a token bucket per tenant and audience (guest/public, staff, service, partner) with counts shared through Azure Managed Redis, sustained rate and a 2x burst for 10 seconds from the tenant's plan (Plan.requestLimits) or the platform default; one tenant held to 25% of a replica's request slots only while the replica is above 70% of its limit; shedding guest and public first, staff and service last (ADR-0032); 429 with Retry-After and the RateLimit-* headers; if Redis is unavailable each replica falls back to its own in-process buckets (the limit divided by the replica count). Done when: in a test with two tenants on one replica, the busy tenant gets the whole replica while the other is quiet, is held to 25% of the slots once the replica passes 70% while the quiet tenant's requests still succeed, a guest burst never spends a till's staff budget, and stopping Redis leaves requests served under the in-process limits.

subject: [BE] Outbox, relay and inbox behind the kernel broker interface, on a local RabbitMQ
description: Outbox, relay and inbox behind the kernel broker interface, on a local RabbitMQ. The transactional outbox per tenant database; one relay per region in the workers host, with a lease and a polling loop per tenant database, and an inbox per tenant database for exactly-once handling (ADR-0058); modules enqueue through IOutbox inside their own transaction, the relay publishes through IBrokerPublisher and consumers subscribe through IEventSubscriber (ADR-0058 amendment, 1 October); the relay drains a full batch at once and its batch size is configuration (Relay:BatchSize, 1,000 in the flash-sale environment). The broker per ADR-0057 is the client's choice between RabbitMQ and Kafka: build behind the kernel interface on a local RabbitMQ until they answer, with ordering per aggregate by an ordering key and dead letters drained into platform.dead_letter. A relay-lag dashboard and alert per tenant database (SD-030, SD-031, SD-032). Done when: an event written in a transaction reaches its consumer once, survives a relay restart and a redelivery, a poison message lands in platform.dead_letter, and relay lag shows on the dashboard and alerts when unpublished rows are older than 60 seconds.

subject: [BE] The on-sale waiting room: Redis positions, the cached page, the release controller, admission tokens
description: The on-sale waiting room: Redis positions, the cached page, the release controller, admission tokens. ADR-0066 (accepted 1 October; B1, or Block A if an on-sale is booked in Block A): enterWaitingRoom gives a position from a Redis counter with no database write; the static branded waiting page is served from Front Door's cache and polls getWaitingRoomPosition; a release controller admits guests per second from the health of commerce (latency and the 429 rate, ADR-0064); an admitted guest gets a short-lived signed token (tenant, performance, expiry, unique id; key in Key Vault) that middleware checks by signature, with no database read, on addCartLine and acquireInventoryHold from guest channels only (till, kiosk and workstation holds are exempt, amendment of 1 October); activation follows the performance's onSaleFrom/onSaleTo or setWaitingRoomSetting. Done when: with the room on, a guest cart hold without a token is refused 403 admission-required, one with a valid token succeeds, a forged or expired token or one for another performance is refused, a till hold needs no token, and the release rate drops when commerce latency rises.

subject: [FE] PTR-041 Commercial Agreement 360°, Health & AI Review
description: Give management a single consolidated view of the complete commercial relationship with a partner. Board 3 manages the day-to-day operational and financial relationship with active B2B, reseller and OTA partners. The three boards now form a clean lifecycle: Board 1 — Who is the partner? Onboarding → Organization → Users → Territory → Compliance → Permissions → Activation Board 2 — Under what commercial terms can they transact? Agreement → Rates → Commission → Credit → Security → Billing → Allocation → Limits Board 3 — What happens once the partner starts doing business? Orders → Reservations → Cancellations → Statements → Reconciliation → Commission Settlement → Disputes → Performance → Risk → AI Optimization A key principle for Board 3 is that it should provide a Partner Operations 360° without rebuilding functionality already owned by Orders, Finance, Ticketing, Payment or Channel Management. Module: Partners. App: Partner Portal.
